title.en: Generation and conduction of the nerve impulse

hook.en: A *nerve impulse* is not electricity flowing down a wire. It is a wave of sodium ions rushing into the axon, one patch after the next, like a Mexican wave in a cricket stadium.
hook.kn: ನರ ಆವೇಗ ತಂತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಹರಿಯುವ ವಿದ್ಯುತ್ ಅಲ್ಲ. ಕ್ರಿಕೆಟ್ ಕ್ರೀಡಾಂಗಣದ ಮೆಕ್ಸಿಕನ್ ಅಲೆಯಂತೆ, ಸೋಡಿಯಂ ಅಯಾನುಗಳು ಒಂದು ಭಾಗದ ನಂತರ ಇನ್ನೊಂದು ಭಾಗದಲ್ಲಿ ಆಕ್ಸಾನ್ ಒಳಗೆ ನುಗ್ಗುವ ಅಲೆ ಅದು.

title.en: Explain the resting membrane potential and the Na+–K+ pump
Explain how the impulse moves along the axon

say.en: A nerve impulse is not electricity flowing down a wire. It is a wave of sodium ions rushing into the axon, one patch after the next, like a Mexican wave in a cricket stadium. In this lesson: Explain the resting membrane potential and the Na plus -K plus pump.
Describe depolarisation and repolarisation.
Explain how the impulse moves along the axon.

body.en: Neurons are excitable cells because their membranes are in a polarised state. Different types of ion channels are present on the neural membrane, selectively permeable to different ions. When a neuron is not conducting an impulse (resting), the axonal membrane is comparatively more permeable to potassium ions (K+) and nearly impermeable to sodium ions (Na+), and it is impermeable to the negatively charged proteins in the axoplasm. So the axoplasm has a high concentration of K+ and negatively charged proteins and a low concentration of Na+, while the fluid outside has a low K+ and a high Na+ concentration — a concentration gradient. These gradients are maintained by the sodium–potassium pump, which actively transports 3 Na+ outwards for 2 K+ into the cell. As a result the outer surface of the axonal membrane has a positive charge and the inner surface is negative: it is polarised. The electrical potential difference across the *resting membrane* is the resting potential.
body.kn: ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಆಕ್ಸಾನ್ ಪೊರೆ K+ ಗೆ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಪ್ರವೇಶ್ಯ, Na+ ಗೆ ಬಹುತೇಕ ಅಪ್ರವೇಶ್ಯ. ಒಳಗೆ K+ ಮತ್ತು ಋಣಾವೇಶದ ಪ್ರೋಟೀನ್‌ಗಳು ಹೆಚ್ಚು, ಹೊರಗೆ Na+ ಹೆಚ್ಚು. ಸೋಡಿಯಂ-ಪೊಟ್ಯಾಸಿಯಂ ಪಂಪ್ 3 Na+ ಹೊರಗೆ ಮತ್ತು 2 K+ ಒಳಗೆ ಸಾಗಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಹೊರಮೈ ಧನ, ಒಳಮೈ ಋಣ — ಇದೇ ಧ್ರುವೀಕೃತ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ ಮತ್ತು ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತಿ ವಿಭವ.

points.en: Inside: high K+, negative proteins; outside: high Na+

narration.en: The teacher draws the polarised membrane, the action-potential graph and the local currents that carry the impulse along the axon.

say.en: At rest the membrane is polarised: positive outside, negative inside. Inside there is more potassium and negative protein; outside more sodium.
The sodium–potassium pump keeps these gradients: it pushes three sodium ions out for every two potassium ions it brings in.
A stimulus opens sodium channels. Sodium rushes in and the inside becomes positive: the action potential. Then potassium leaves and the resting potential returns.
The impulse travels because the depolarised spot A drives local currents to the next spot B, which then fires too.
The teacher draws the polarised membrane, the action-potential graph and the local currents that carry the impulse along the axon.

caption.en: At rest the inside of the axon is negative (about −70 mV). A stimulus strong enough to reach threshold (about −55 mV) opens Na+ channels: Na+ rushes in and the inside becomes positive (depolarisation). Then K+ moves out and the resting state returns (repolarisation). Weaker stimuli give no impulse: it is all or none.
caption.kn: ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಆಕ್ಸಾನ್ ಒಳಭಾಗ ಋಣ (ಸುಮಾರು −70 mV). ಮಿತಿ (ಸುಮಾರು −55 mV) ತಲುಪುವ ಪ್ರಚೋದನೆ Na+ ನಾಳಗಳನ್ನು ತೆರೆಯುತ್ತದೆ: ಒಳಭಾಗ ಧನ (ವಿಧ್ರುವೀಕರಣ). ನಂತರ K+ ಹೊರಹೋಗಿ ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತಿ ಸ್ಥಿತಿ ಮರಳುತ್ತದೆ. ಎಲ್ಲಾ ಅಥವಾ ಏನೂ ಇಲ್ಲ.

body.en: When a stimulus is applied at a site (say A) on the polarised membrane, the membrane there becomes freely permeable to Na+. This leads to a rapid influx of Na+ followed by reversal of the polarity: the outer surface becomes negative and the inner surface positive. The membrane at A is now depolarised. The electrical potential difference across it is the *action potential*, which is in fact termed a nerve impulse. At the next site (B) the outer surface is still positive and the inner surface negative, so a current flows on the inner surface from A to B and on the outer surface from B to A. The polarity at B is reversed and an action potential is generated there; the impulse is thus conducted along the axon. The rise in stimulus-induced permeability to Na+ is extremely short-lived. It is quickly followed by a rise in permeability to K+; within a fraction of a second K+ diffuses outside the membrane and restores the resting potential at the site of excitation. The fibre becomes once more responsive to further stimulation.
body.kn: ಉದ್ದೀಪನ ನೀಡಿದಾಗ ಪೊರೆ Na+ ಗೆ ಮುಕ್ತವಾಗಿ ಪ್ರವೇಶ್ಯವಾಗಿ Na+ ಒಳನುಗ್ಗುತ್ತದೆ; ಧ್ರುವತೆ ತಿರುಗುತ್ತದೆ — ಇದೇ ವಿಧ್ರುವೀಕರಣ. ಈ ವಿಭವ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವೇ ಕ್ರಿಯಾವಿಭವ ಅಥವಾ ನರ ಆವೇಗ. ನಂತರ K+ ಹೊರಹೋಗಿ ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತಿ ವಿಭವ ಮರುಸ್ಥಾಪಿತವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಹೀಗೆ ಆವೇಗ ಆಕ್ಸಾನ್ ಉದ್ದಕ್ಕೂ ಸಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

problem.en: A resting axon is stimulated at point A. Describe the state of the membrane at A and at a neighbouring point B (a) just after stimulation and (b) a fraction of a second later.

steps.en: (a) At A: Na+ rushes in, so the outer surface is negative and the inner surface positive (depolarised). At B: still polarised, outside positive and inside negative.
Local currents flow on the inner surface from A to B and on the outer surface from B to A, which depolarises B.
(b) At A: K+ permeability rises, K+ diffuses out and the resting potential is restored. At B: now depolarised — the action potential has moved on.

answer.en: The depolarised zone moves from A to B while A repolarises, so the impulse travels along the axon

say.en: Let us work this out together. A resting axon is stimulated at point A. Describe the state of the membrane at A and at a neighbouring point B a just after stimulation and b a fraction of a second later.
a At A: Na plus rushes in, so the outer surface is negative and the inner surface positive depolarised. At B: still polarised, outside positive and inside negative.
Local currents flow on the inner surface from A to B and on the outer surface from B to A, which depolarises B.
b At A: K plus permeability rises, K plus diffuses out and the resting potential is restored. At B: now depolarised, the action potential has moved on.
So the answer is The depolarised zone moves from A to B while A repolarises, so the impulse travels along the axon.

At rest the axoplasm has high K⁺ and negative proteins and low Na⁺; the membrane is more permeable to K⁺; the pump moves 3 Na⁺ out for 2 kelvin⁺ in, so the outside is positive.
